The following sample statements may be helpful in crafting statements tailored to the learning goals of specific courses: Before beginning your studies at Notre Dame, you signed the Honor Code pledge, affirming that you would not tolerate or participate in academic dishonesty, and this includes the appropriate use of generative AI tools. For the purposes of this class, you may not engage in unauthorized collaboration to complete any work for the course, and you may not use any generative AI composition or editing tools, unless it is specifically permitted for the assignment. AI composition or editing software (like ChatGPT or Grammarly) may not be used for assignments in this course unless specifically stated in the assignment. Using these tools without my permission puts your academic integrity at risk. When this use has been permitted, the content generated or modified by AI must be properly attributed. The use of AI tools is generally acceptable in this course, but, like any other source, must always be attributed in a manner that can be reproduced by the reader.
units.why: AI must be attributed "like any other source ... in a manner that can be reproduced by the reader": the rule is to attribute, P24.
units.fit_note: Also treats AI like any other source (P45), which the type does not capture.

units.passage: When quoting or closely paraphrasing AI output, mark it as such and provide attribution.
units.why: Open sample: quoted or closely paraphrased AI output must be marked and attributed (P24).
units.fit_note: Applies to quoted or paraphrased text, not code.

units.passage: Encourage your students to use proper citations. Communicate your preferred method of citation to them.
units.why: Instructors should "Encourage your students to use proper citations" and communicate a preferred method, a disclosure/citation expectation (P24).
units.fit_note: Phrased as encouragement to faculty, not a requirement for students.

units.passage: Be clear with students, both verbally and in written policies, as to when it is appropriate to use these tools for your courses and whether and how they should disclose that they used them.
units.why: 'Be clear with students ... whether and how they should disclose that they used them' asks instructors to state a disclosure rule, so P24, instructor, course-start, should. It is a distinct rule from the preceding 'when it is appropriate' instruction.
units.fit_note: Leaves disclosure rules to the instructor; sets no disclosure duty itself.
